messages:
maria: @here seeing a weird one — gpu pods for the realtime model are PENDING even though nodepools show available GPU nodes. CA didn't scale up. :thinking_face:
ajay: can you paste the pod yaml? are they using nodeAffinity or a specific toleration?
sam: also check taints on the nodes, we recently added gpu:exclusive=true:NoSchedule to isolate inference workloads
maria: pasted below — the pods use tolerations: operator Exists and a nodeSelector for gpu-type: a100. Pods are Pending with Reason: '0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't match node selector.'
maria: node labels on pool-a100-spot: gpu-type=a100, gpu=present, gpu.redwood.com/exclusive=true
ajay: hmm if nodeSelector matches but scheduler says didn't match, maybe it's namespace label or typo in key?
lee: another common thing — cluster-autoscaler won't scale up if pods have podAffinity requiredDuringScheduling and it can't satisfy. any required affinities?
maria: no podAffinity, just tolerations. Also CA logs show: 'NoScaleUpCandidatesFound: pods ineligible for scale-up: pod requires node label that does not exist on any node group'
sam: oh — we renamed the label from gpu-type to gpu.redwood.com/type last week for Dedicated pools. If the pod uses gpu-type it won't match new nodepool labels.
maria: argh. that explains the 0/10 nodes message. However, even after relabeling, CA still hesitates to scale new on-demand nodes because we have a mix of spot and on-demand nodegroups and expander is set to 'most-pods'.
ajay: we should avoid manual nodeSelector keys; prefer nodeAffinity with preferredDuringScheduling so CA can still pick compatible pool. also consider using label aliasing in our admission controller to map older keys to new ones.
sam: quick patch idea — add a toleration-only fallback pool: nodes labeled gpu.redwood.com/exclusive=false and toleration operator Exists so less-restricted pods can land there when strict label isn't available. But that changes isolation guarantees.
lee: for isolation + scaling, we use taint gpu.redwood.com/slots=exclusive:NoSchedule on exclusive pools and pods that need isolation add toleration with key and value:Equal. Example toleration snippet: ```yaml
 tolerations:
 - key: "gpu.redwood.com/slots"
   operator: "Equal"
   value: "exclusive"
   effect: "NoSchedule"
```
maria: thanks. two followups: (1) should infra revert the label rename or add aliasing? (2) how do we make CA respect spot vs on-demand preferences but still scale when needed without breaking isolation?
ajay: (1) add a small admission controller that copies gpu.redwood.com/type -> gpu-type if missing, fast and low blast. (2) change CA expander to 'least-waste' or 'price' with a node-group priority list and enable balance-similar-node-groups. Also tune scale-up-delay and unneeded-time to be shorter for GPU pools to improve responsiveness.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: When realtime GPU pods Pending > 2m and CA logs show 'NoScaleUpCandidatesFound', check 1) node label mismatch 2) requiredDuringScheduling affinities 3) taint/toleration operator mismatch. If label mismatch, create label alias or update pod selector.
maria: going to add the admission mapping and redeploy realtime helm chart to use gpu.redwood.com/type. I'll also open a ticket to tweak CA expander and add a tiny fallback pool with looser taint but tagged with billing:high-cost=true so we can track cost impact.
sam: ping me for the ticket, I can prototype the admission mapping today. :thumbsup:
lee: after patch, let's run a small canary scale test: create 3 pods with gpu:redwood.com/type=a100 and ensure CA scales the pool and pods land on exclusive nodes, then drain a node to test eviction & safe-to-evict annotation behavior.
maria: agreed. I'll coordinate and post results here. Thanks everyone :rocket:
